transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-14
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Joanna Li (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Michael Bennett (Horizon Head of AI), Priya Shah (Horizon Director Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Horizon Platform SRE), Aisha Khan (Horizon Product)

Summary: QBR / health check. Discussed rising token spend, a recent flurry of 5xxs during peak, proposal to pilot Dedicated capacity and a VPC/private plan for PII customers. Agreed next steps around pricing, tests, and a performance deep dive.

[00:00] Joanna: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh welcome to our QBR, I think we've got about 45 minutes locked, we'll go through usage, cost, reliability, and then roadmap items, and leave some time for questions. Michael, Priya, thanks for being here.
[00:18] Michael: Yeah thanks Jo, appreciate it. Quick note, we had some execs ask about the spike in spend the last month so hopefully we can get into details.
[00:25] Samir: Yeah we'll walk through the billing trends and also show you a few levers — batching suggestions, quantify options, um quant profiles — that can bring per-token costs down.
[00:35] Priya: Also curious about the Dedicated proposal; if we reserve we need guar- guaranteed latency at 99th, that's the ask from infra.
[00:45] Elena: Totally. For Dedicated we can size the GPU pool and set SLOs. In practice we see 99th down to low hundreds of milliseconds for short seqs, longer seqs vary. We'll run a targeted bench for your workload.
[01:05] Carlos: Last incident — around Feb 27 — we saw a cascade of 502s when our traffic spiked. Can someone recap what the root cause was?
[01:15] Joanna: Yep, we pulled the incident report, it looks like a combination of an unexpected prefix pattern causing KV cache misses and aggressive autoscaler back-and-forth during the burst. The runtime's batching behavior interacted oddly with the request fan-out.
[01:33] Elena: To add, there was also a kernel fallback on a minority of max-len requests that temporarily bumped latencies which tripped the autoscaler thresholds. We're proposing a couple mitigations: fixed minimum capacity for peak windows and improved prefix caching settings for your common prompts.
[01:58] Michael: When you say prefix caching — is that the KV cache? We've got a few prompts with user PII, how is that handled for caching on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[02:10] Samir: Good question. By default we don't persist customer PII in shared caches; for Dedicated we can enable customer-scoped KV cache or disable prefix caching for sensitive flows. For Private/VPC deployments, you control the cache and keys via your KMS.
[02:28] Priya: That sounds promising. Any compliance attestations for the private option? SOC 2 and ISO? Also auditors asked about audit logs retention.
[02:38] Joanna: We have SOC 2 and ISO attestations; we also provide audit log exports and day-one integration with common SIEMs. I'll send the security pack after the call.
[02:47] Aisha: Also, curious about data residency — some EU customers require EU-only. We are planning to onboard a new EU retail partner.
[02:55] Elena: We support region pinning and private deployments in EU regions; for Private on-prem, obviously you control residency.
[03:05] Michael: Back to cost — your billing dashboard shows a 42% increase in tokens month-over-month, what's driving it?
[03:12] Samir: We correlated it to new feature rollout in January — chat reply expansion and more contextual history per request. Also error retries during the Feb incident inflated tokens. We'll send a cleaned token distribution and recommended retention / truncation policy.
[03:30] Priya: Can you model the committed reserved cost vs pay-as-you-go for our numbers? We want to see break-even horizon.
[03:37] Samir: Yep — I'll send two scenarios: 12-month commit and 3-month burst plan with autoscale. We'll include both per-token unit economics and overall monthly spend.
[03:45] Carlos: On the performance deep dive, we want to include our dev dataset. Can Elena work with us to run a 1k sample?
[03:52] Elena: Absolutely. If you can share a redacted dataset and an access key we can run it in a private test cluster and provide P95/P99 numbers.
[04:02] Michael: Any callouts on model variants? We currently use an open model that Redwood hosts, are there lighter variants for non-critical flows?
[04:10] Joanna: Yes we often recommend fallback to a lower-cost variant for lower-sensitivity paths. Also quantized model variants can drop costs substantially with small quality tradeoffs.
[04:20] Priya: How much can batching help? Our traffic has lots of short single-turn requests during peak windows.
[04:27] Elena: Batching helps your throughput and unit cost if latency SLOs allow for a small queuing window. For short requests batching gains are modest but combined with KV caching and prefix deduping, we typically see 15-30% token-cost reduction.
[04:45] Carlos: Is there a recommended minimum Dedicated size to avoid autoscaler thrash?
[04:52] Elena: For your peak QPS based on what you sent us, a minimum pool of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs with burst capacity set to 12 during black friday-like peaks should be a good starting point; we'll refine after the tests.
[05:10] Michael: Security — are there HSM integrations for key management?
[05:16] Samir: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support KMS/HSM integrations. For Hosted you can bring your own key via partner KMS in most cases.
[05:26] Priya: Great. Any blockers from finance on reserved pricing and invoicing?
[05:31] Joanna: We can do monthly or annual invoicing; if you need PO terms we'll route to sales ops. Samir will include contract language options.
[05:40] Aisha: Roadmap wise, any ETA on the Optimize recommendations UI? That would help our ops team tune batching without deep platform changes.
[05:48] Joanna: We plan to roll out the UI Q2, with a beta in late April. We'll invite Horizon to that beta.
[05:55] Michael: Okay next steps recap?
[06:00] Joanna: Samir sends pricing and committed usage models; Elena sets up the 1k test and bench with Carlos; Priya sends token distribution; Joanna sends security pack and schedules the deep dive for 2026-03-22.
[06:12] Priya: Sounds good. One last quick question — do you have any references or case studies for retailers using Dedicated?
[06:20] Samir: Yep I'll share two retailer case studies and a short architecture note.
[06:25] Michael: Thanks everyone.
[06:28] Joanna: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and owners.
[06:32] (call ends)

Note: transcript contains minor automatic transcription errors and occasional speaker label drift; product names sometimes shortened (e.g., Redwood Dedicate / Redwood Dedicated pool) and technical terms like KV cache occasionally transcribed as "KV cash" or "KV cache miss".
